description:
I have a feeling this is in Moraceae.  Not sure if it’s some kind of a Mulberry, but the leaves are not like any Mulberry I’ve seen.  Growing by the outer edge of Alley Pond park, on the north western side, by the street.

iNat AI is utterly confused and thinks it's a Maple.  The leaves are alternate, not opposite. 

I have been mulling, as in "(mul)berry", over this phenotype for about a week, ever since I found a similar looking plant in Alley Pond Park.

I did some searching on gbif.org and looked through hundreds of herbarium specimens.

The closest match I found was this one, collected in Taiwan in 1982, and stored at the University of Florida herbarium (Florida Museum of Natural History):
Morus australis (Wild Korean Mulberry)
https://www.gbif.org/occurrence/1457825768

It seems that iNaturalist treats M. australis and M. indica as synonyms.

Here is another iNat observation that looks very similar to this plant:

Morus indica
https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/70645134
